judged_text: The newly inserted block performs a token-refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com plus an unconditional prisma.credential.update every time the jsforce connection is created, with no expiry check and no APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED guard — previously the connection was built purely from stored credentials with no network or DB write. Every calendar operation that creates the service/connection (availability checks, booking flows) now pays a remote round-trip plus a credential-table write even when the stored token is still valid, adding latency to the booking hot path and causing concurrent operations to race on rewriting the same credential row; it also means the stripping corruption reaches stored data on first use, not just on natural token expiry.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional token refresh (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token" ...)`) and an unconditional `prisma.credential.update(...)` before constructing the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no expiry/validity check in the shown code and it does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (which is where the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`/`CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` gating lives). This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavioral change that can add latency and extra DB writes/races on any code path that instantiates the service/connection, but it’s primarily a performance/architecture concern rather than a clearly provable functional defect from the diff alone.
